correctness.rationale: Independent uniform parent and pre-existing removal draws give offspring type-1 probability x+μ(1−2x), x=k/n; multiplying with the opposite removal probabilities gives the two stated off-diagonal entries. Reflection is legitimate by allele symmetry. At the top it adds both jump probabilities when n is even and makes the original upward jump a hold when n is odd. Below the top p+q is at most 1−2x(1−x)<1, so holding is positive, and downward probabilities are positive even at μ=1. Finiteness and positive descending paths give eventual absorption with a geometric upper bound. By skip-free motion and the strong Markov property, starting one step higher adds a nonnegative first-passage time in distribution, so each survival vector is nondecreasing with initial minority count. The derivative D favors up over down on those vectors, with zero top row for even n and a nonnegative action at the odd top. Differentiating Q^t gives the sum of nonnegative terms; since D1 has first component (1−2/n)/n>0 for n>=3, the j=0 term reaches any r by t>=r using r−1 downward steps and arbitrary positive holds. Hence survival is one for t<r and strictly increasing in μ at every other horizon, endpoints included by integration. Summing finite means proves strict mean ordering. The primitive killed matrix has simple Perron root in (0,1). Its positive right Perron vector is a limit of rescaled nondecreasing survival vectors, so Dv is nonnegative with first component at least (1−2/n)v_1/n>0. The simple-root derivative w^T Dv/(w^T v) is therefore positive, including one-sided endpoint derivatives; the left and right Perron vectors give the positive survival prefactor. The one-state matrices at n=2 and 3 yield respectively 1/2 and (7+μ)/9. An independently written integer replay on the full allele count (python3 /workspace/branches/frozen_math_replay.py 5) used literal ordered individual draws and mutation weights; 1872 adjacent-rate comparisons passed, n=2..9, μ=j/4, t=0..12, including both small-size formulas. The reported exact-rational checks of the inspected supplied script cover other finite cases; the Perron conclusion is established by the proof, not by either computation.

value.rationale: In a natural finite neutral model, strict comparison of the whole first-homogeneity law is stronger than comparison of its mean. It holds for the entire flip range even though mutation increases the probability of any allele-count change away from the central count. The order starts exactly at the first reachable horizon and has a sharp population-size boundary. The strict Perron derivative also resolves sensitivity of the asymptotic survival scale, which does not follow just from ordering finite horizons. This is about temporary pure-state entrance and does not claim biological fixation in a system with continuing mutation.
